title: Pinegrove Warehousing — LLM selection and tool-calling scout
summary: Discovery call to understand Pinegrove's requirements for model selection across hosted/dedicated/private deployment modes. Focus: large context for order history (>=64k tokens), multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), and tool-calling to inventory/ERP systems. Security constraints around KMS and on-prem data retention. Next steps include benchmark plan, security docs, and pricing for a small Dedicated pilot.
topics: tool-calling to internal inventory API and SQL backends
hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
security: KMS, SOC2, audit logs, VPC
latency vs cost and batching strategies

transcript: [00:00] Jordan Hale: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Tom Li: Tom here, CTO at Pinegrove.
[00:09] Carlos Mendes: Carlos, head of ML.
[00:11] Aisha Khan: Aisha from platform engineering.
[00:13] Leah Ortiz: Leah, data ops.
[00:15] Raj Patel: Raj, consulting on infra.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya, SE — I'll be taking notes on architecture and benchmarks. Marcus and Sophie are also on the call for product/solutions context.

[00:28] Jordan Hale: Great. Goal for today is to understand your drivers — are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for the inference stack, and what model characteristics matter (context length, multilingual, tool-calling). Carlos, can you give us a quick use-case walkthrough?

[00:40] Carlos Mendes: Sure. At Pinegrove we run warehouse management and order reconciliation. We want an assistant that can ingest long order histories and generate root-cause across weeks of logs — like 30–60k tokens for a single session. We also need Spanish and Portuguese support; about 25% of users are Spanish-speaking. And crucially, we want the model to call our inventory APIs and run SQL queries so it can check stock levels and open tickets automatically.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Got it. So long context, multilingual, and tool-calling. Do you have any existing latency SLOs for these user interactions?

[01:12] Aisha Khan: Ideally sub-800ms for short queries, but for these longer analyses 1.5–3s per token is fine as long as throughput is predictable. We are more sensitive to tail latency — spikes mess up downstream workflows.
[01:26] Jordan Hale: That helps. On security, are you able to send logs to a managed KMS or do you need on-prem key material?

[01:33] Tom Li: We have a corporate KMS in our cloud account but for certain workflows we need to keep customer PII in our VPC and prefer Private deployment. Also SOC2 compliance is a must, and we need detailed audit logs of prompts and model responses for a 3rd-party audit in Q2.

[01:49] Jordan Hale: Understood. Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs in both Dedicated and Private modes; Hosted can be configured for restricted retention but Private gives you full control. We'll share the SOC2 package and specifics about audit logs.
[01:58] Leah Ortiz: Quick Q — in Dedicated, can we pin a model revision and prevent auto-upgrades? We need deterministic behavior for compliance.
[02:05] Marcus Lee: Yes — Dedicated and Private support model pinning and controlled rollouts. You can do canary deploys and A/B test, and you decide when to apply an updated binary or model weights.
[02:15] Raj Patel: On the model front, what are Redwood's recommended open models for long-context, multilingual, and tool-calling?

[02:21] Priya Nair: We typically evaluate Mistral variants for strong base performance, Llama-family models (3 and optimized forks) for tool-calling and structured output, and Falcon/RedPajama derivatives for some tasks. For long context, commercial forks or special tokenizers and KV-cache tweaks are important. We also look at quantized 4-bit variants when cost is a concern.
[02:44] Carlos Mendes: We've been testing Llama2-70B but it struggles past 32k and gets expensive. Any recommended path to 64k?

[02:52] Priya Nair: There are two orthogonal approaches: model selection (some newer architectures scale better with attention mechanisms), and runtime/engine tricks — chunked attention, FlashAttention variants, and sharded KV cache across GPUs. Redwood's runtime supports larger context by adjusting kernel selection, and for Dedicated we can provision more GPU memory or use model variants with rotary/ALiBi tweaks. We'll propose models and configs in the bench plan.
[03:14] Aisha Khan: For tool-calling, we need the model to reliably invoke our inventory API and then parse the JSON result. How do you handle deterministic tool outputs?

[03:23] Priya Nair: We support function-calling style where the model emits structured JSON or a schema. Our runtime enforces schema validation and we can set higher temperature=0 baselines and system prompts to improve determinism. For mission-critical flows, we'd suggest a verification step — call the API, validate response, and if uncertain, re-run with additional context.
[03:41] Tom Li: How much of the integration is on our side vs Redwood side? We want to minimize infra changes.

[03:47] Jordan Hale: For Hosted, you push tool endpoints to us (webhooks) and we handle routing. For Dedicated/Private, tool-calling runs in your network boundary (VPC connectors or on-prem proxies) if you prefer. We typically provide an SDK and example connectors — Marcus will share a repo.
[03:59] Marcus Lee: I'll drop the link after the call — simple examples for Node/Python that show function calling and a SQL proxy.
[04:05] Carlos Mendes: Cost — what does 64k context look like in Hosted vs Dedicated?

[04:10] Jordan Hale: With Hosted, cost per token is higher because we absorb variability and scale. Dedicated shifts unit economics to your committed capacity — cheaper per-token at steady state. For pilots, Hosted is fastest to test; for production with predictable QPS, Dedicated is usually more economical. We'll send a side-by-side estimate.
[04:25] Aisha Khan: Spike question — if we have bursty traffic, can Dedicated handle bursts?

[04:30] Priya Nair: Yes, you can configure burst capacity and autoscaling bands. There's also a fallback routing policy to Hosted models if Dedicated capacity is exhausted — depends on your tolerance for routing to a different model variant.
[04:41] Leah Ortiz: About multilingual benchmarks — any models that handle Spanish/Portuguese well out of the box?

[04:47] Priya Nair: Mistral offerings and certain Llama-derivatives with multilingual fine-tuning usually do well; we will include ensembling and prompt templates in the bench plan. We'll test for hallucination rates in Spanish for your domain-specific vocabulary.
[05:00] Tom Li: We also have legal constraints in BR and EU — data residency matters. Can Redwood run Dedicated in a region within EU?
[05:07] Jordan Hale: Yes, Dedicated pools can be regionally located. Private deployment obviously offers full on-prem control. We'll map regions and available capacity in the follow-up.

[05:15] Carlos Mendes: On eval metrics — aside from latency and cost, we want recall on retrieval and tool-calling accuracy, plus hallucination rate under multi-turn contexts. Can Redwood instrument those?

[05:24] Sophie Tran: Redwood Optimize and Console can track custom evals and regression alerts. We can hook your prompt sets and track metrics over time — send us initial eval prompts and we'll wire it up in the PoC.
[05:36] Raj Patel: Any known gotchas when pushing long document contexts — tokenization boundaries, truncation, or embeddings limitations?

[05:43] Priya Nair: Tokenization surprises happen — some embeddings or retrieval pipelines chunk differently. We suggest a pre-processing step that preserves semantic units and align chunk sizes to the model's context window. Also watch for KV cache invalidation if you frequently switch model variants mid-session.

[05:59] Jordan Hale: Let's talk concrete pilot scope: propose a 2-week Dedicated pilot with 8 GPUs, run benchmarks at 32k/64k, test tool-calling to sample inventory API, and evaluate Spanish/Portuguese prompts. Thoughts?

[06:12] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. For the pilot success criteria: 1) tool-calls succeed 95%+ on a set of 250 queries, 2) sub-2s median response on routine queries, and 3) hallucination rate under 3% for the eval set.
[06:26] Priya Nair: We'll aim to meet those. For the 95% tool-call success, we'll pair deterministic function-calling templates and schema checks.
[06:32] Aisha Khan: Networking question — for Private, do you require any special ports or do you support private peering?
[06:38] Marcus Lee: We support VPC peering, private links, and on-prem connectors via a small footprint agent. We'll share the network checklist.
[06:45] Tom Li: What about data retention and redaction? We can't store raw PII outside our control.

[06:50] Jordan Hale: For Dedicated/Private you control retention. Hosted can be configured for ephemeral logs, but for compliance Private/Dedicated is preferred. We also support server-side redaction rules and can mask PII before storage.
[07:00] Leah Ortiz: Are there any open-source runtime performance hits we should expect compared to Redwood's runtime optimizations?

[07:06] Priya Nair: Open-source runtimes can work but they often lack the kernel-level optimizations and continuous batching of Redwood's runtime. That yields higher latency and cost. For long-context loads, our kernel selection and KV cache sharding reduce memory blowup.
[07:22] Carlos Mendes: Regarding models — can we bring our own fine-tuned weights?
[07:27] Jordan Hale: Yes. Both Dedicated and Private allow you to upload and pin custom weights. We'll validate format and compatibility; Priya will include the upload checklist in the bench plan.
[07:35] Aisha Khan: Any recommendation on quantization for 64k contexts? Is 4-bit safe for our use-case?

[07:41] Priya Nair: 4-bit quant is good for many workloads but watch for subtle quality regression on instruction-following and tool extraction. We'll test 4-bit and q4_0 variants as part of the bench — often a mixed strategy (higher precision for decoder layers) works best.
[07:55] Tom Li: Can Redwood support a hybrid — Dedicated for core flows and Hosted fallback during spikes?
[07:59] Jordan Hale: Absolutely. Smart routing policies enable that. You can route based on latency, cost thresholds, or capacity; fallbacks can use cheaper model variants for non-critical queries.
[08:09] Marcus Lee: I'll include examples of routing policies in the follow-up pack.
[08:13] Carlos Mendes: One last technical: when the model calls SQL, can Redwood help with query safety to avoid destructive statements?

[08:20] Priya Nair: Yes — we recommend a proxy layer that enforces read-only roles for model-driven queries and a query sanitizer. Redwood has an example SQL proxy that limits verbs and enforces parameterization.
